original_question: Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system and let u <= v in W. If ~Phi_{u,v}(c,d) denotes the complete cd-index of the Bruhat interval [u,v], must all coefficients of ~Phi_{u,v} be nonnegative?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Conjecture 1.8: for every Coxeter system (W,S) and every pair u,v ∈ W with u ≤ v, the complete cd-index is conjectured to have nonnegative coefficients; in the paper this is stated as widetilde{Phi}_{u,v} ∈ N⟨c,d⟩. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already isolates the correct object (the complete cd-index of the Bruhat interval [u,v]), the correct ambient combinatorial setting (a Coxeter system and Bruhat order), and the correct property (coefficientwise nonnegativity). It is therefore aimed at exactly Conjecture 1.8 rather than a broader neighboring Kazhdan-Lusztig problem. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
missing_details: The paper formulates the conjecture as membership in the free associative algebra/semiring: one should specify that widetilde{Phi}_{u,v}(c,d) lies in Z⟨c,d⟩ with c and d noncommuting, and the claim is that in fact widetilde{Phi}_{u,v} ∈ N⟨c,d⟩. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))

To make the notation stand-alone, one should define widetilde{Phi}_{u,v} by the identity widetilde{psi}_{u,v}(a,b)=widetilde{Phi}_{u,v}(a+b,ab+ba), where a and b are also noncommuting variables. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))

The paper defines widetilde{psi}_{u,v}(a,b) as a sum over directed paths in the Bruhat graph, using a reflection ordering; this is part of the intended meaning of the complete cd-index and is implicit in your draft. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
The order relation u ≤ v should be stated explicitly to be Bruhat order. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))

The nearby context fixes the grading deg(a)=deg(b)=deg(c)=1 and deg(d)=2, and notes that the top homogeneous part of widetilde{Phi}_{u,v} has degree ℓ(u,v)-1 and is the ordinary cd-index of [u,v]; this is not the conjecture itself, but it is part of the paper's precise setup for the phrase 'complete cd-index.' ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
refined_question: For every Coxeter system (W,S) and every u,v ∈ W with u ≤ v in Bruhat order, let widetilde{psi}_{u,v}(a,b)=Σ_Γ m_≺(Γ), where Γ ranges over directed paths u=x0 →^{t1} x1 → ··· →^{tk} xk=v in the Bruhat graph, ≺ is a reflection ordering on the set T of reflections, and m_≺(Γ)=y1···y_{k-1} with y_j=a if t_j ≺ t_{j+1} and y_j=b otherwise (and m_≺(Γ)=1 if k=1). Since there is a unique polynomial widetilde{Phi}_{u,v}(c,d) ∈ Z⟨c,d⟩ in noncommuting variables c,d such that widetilde{psi}_{u,v}(a,b)=widetilde{Phi}_{u,v}(a+b,ab+ba), is it always true that widetilde{Phi}_{u,v}(c,d) ∈ N⟨c,d⟩, i.e. that every cd-monomial coefficient of the complete cd-index of the Bruhat interval [u,v] is a nonnegative integer? ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
justification: This is clearly the paper's Conjecture 1.8 in Section 1. The paragraph immediately before Conjecture 1.8 defines the path-sum widetilde{psi}_{u,v}, the complete cd-index widetilde{Phi}_{u,v}, its ambient ring Z⟨c,d⟩, and the grading convention; the conjecture then states exactly widetilde{Phi}_{u,v} ∈ N⟨c,d⟩. Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 provide surrounding Section 1 notation for Kazhdan-Lusztig theory, but the draft's actual target is the later complete-cd-index nonnegativity conjecture, not those earlier theorem-definitions. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
